intro: Searching for will writing near me usually means you want to put your affairs in order without travelling far, and you'd like a straightforward conversation with someone local. Whether you're writing your first will or updating an old one, the right professional can help you set out who inherits what and who takes on the executor role.
need_heading: What people searching for will writing near me usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for will writing near me want a clear, local service to prepare or update a will that reflects their wishes.
needs: You want to make a legally valid will that sets out who inherits your estate and who acts as executor.
You need to name guardians for young children in case something happens to you.
You've married or entered a civil partnership and need to understand how that affects an earlier will.
You've been through a big life event such as divorce, a new child or a bereavement and need to revisit your will.
You'd like to know where your original will is stored and how to keep it safe.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about will writing near me
context: Writing a will is not a reserved legal activity in England and Wales, so some will writers are not regulated. Solicitors regulated by the SRA and chartered legal executives regulated by CILEx are insured and covered by the Legal Ombudsman. Many specialists are also members of STEP or Solicitors for the Elderly.

When you choose a local provider, ask whether they are regulated, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance and where your original will is stored. If you live in Scotland, make sure your adviser practises in the right jurisdiction, as succession rules differ there.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring about will writing near me
tell: Mention that you are looking for will writing near me and give your town or postcode so we can introduce you to a local professional.
Say whether this is your first will or an update to an existing one.
Explain your family situation, including whether you have children and whether you want to name guardians.
List the main assets you want to cover, such as a home, savings or a business.
Mention any recent life events like marriage, divorce or a bereavement that might affect your will.
Ask about where the original will would be stored and whether the professional is regulated and insured.
questions: Are you regulated, and by which body?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Where will my original will be stored, and how can I access it later?
How will you make sure my will is properly signed and witnessed?
What happens if I marry or enter a civil partnership after making my will?
Can you explain how your fees work, even though the quote is on application?

faqs.q: Do I need a solicitor to write a will?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, as will writing is not a reserved legal activity in England and Wales. However, solicitors and chartered legal executives are regulated, insured and covered by the Legal Ombudsman, which gives you extra protection.

faqs.q: How do I find a will writer near me?
faqs.a: You can search for local will writers and ask about their regulation, insurance and where they store original wills. iComply can introduce you to a suitable professional based on what you tell us.

faqs.q: What should I bring to my first meeting?
faqs.a: It helps to bring a list of your assets, details of family members and anyone you want to include, and the names of people you'd like as executors. If you have an existing will, bring that too.

In England and Wales, marriage or entering a civil partnership usually revokes an earlier will, so you should revisit your will after such a life event. Scotland has its own rules, so check with an adviser practising there if that applies to you.
